payload.title: Triton vs cuTile vs PTX-ISA: The Future of AI Hardware Programming
payload.summary: A comprehensive comparison of tile-level programming systems competing to define the next-generation AI accelerator programming middleware.

sections.heading: 1. They All Answer the Same Question
sections.gist: These projects are fundamentally competing for **the middleware layer of next-generation AI accelerator programming**: preventing developers from writing thread-level CUDA or complex manual scheduling, while avoiding regression to fixed-li…

sections.heading: 2. Why Did They Emerge?
sections.gist: AI kernel development over the past decade has progressed through three stages:

sections.heading: 3. Project Positioning Comparison
sections.gist: table columns: Project, Core Position, Abstraction Layer, Greatest Advantage, Greatest Risk/Weakness

sections.heading: 4. cuTile / CUDA Tile: NVIDIA's Official Tile Programming Entry
sections.gist: cuTile is NVIDIA's new Python DSL introduced in the **CUDA 13.x** era, backed by **CUDA Tile IR**.

sections.heading: 5. Triton: The Most Practical Custom GPU Kernel DSL Today
sections.gist: Triton is the **most mature and widely adopted** tool in this category.

sections.heading: 6. TileLang: More Explicit, Targeting Complex Fused Operators
sections.gist: Positioned as "writing high-performance GPU/CPU kernels with Pythonic syntax while retaining low-level optimization capabilities." Built on **TVM compilation infrastructure**.

sections.heading: 7. CuTe DSL: Not to be Confused with cuTile
sections.gist: NVIDIA's ecosystem also contains **CuTe DSL**, part of the CUTLASS family — a Python DSL evolved from C++ CuTe/CUTLASS.

sections.heading: 8. PTO-ISA: Ascend Ecosystem's Tile Virtual ISA
sections.gist: **Ascend CANN-defined Parallel Tile Operation virtual ISA**.

sections.heading: 9. PyPTO: High-Level Tile/Graph Programming on Ascend
sections.gist: A high-performance AI accelerator programming framework based on the PTO paradigm.

sections.heading: 10. TileLang-Ascend: Where TileLang Meets PTO/Ascend
sections.gist: A noteworthy branch: a high-level tile DSL connecting multiple backends.

sections.heading: 12. Limitations Are Also Clear
sections.gist: - **Standard operators may not be worth writing yourself.** Standard GEMM, Conv, LayerNorm, and common attention patterns are already highly optimized in mature libraries.

sections.heading: 13. Future Development Assessment
sections.gist: **2026**: Triton continues as mainstream; cuTile/TileLang/PTO rapidly catching up.

sections.heading: 14. Practical Selection Guidelines
sections.gist: - **NVIDIA + PyTorch custom kernels** → Triton first: fused elementwise, reduction, attention variants, quantization, inference kernels.
